title: Winco , 13-7/8'' x 3-1/8'' Wood Chinois Pestle, Assorted
description:
The food preparation will be easier then ever once you use this chinois pestle.
Made of the solid wood, it is extremely durable and reliable.
Use for crushing and pushing ingredients through strainers.
An ergonomic handle provides with a comfortable grip to make cooking even more convenient.
The shape of the pestle perfectly fits standard-sized strainers.
reviews_5s: She says the size is big and perfect and makes short work of smushing the fruit into pulp for fruit leather. The wood quality is good and no imperfections. My wife thought the handles could be longer but the daughter-in-law says it is fine.This pestle made pushing & rubbing the fruit though the 10" strainer/chinois much, much, much easier. I wanted both the juice and pulp to make raspberry jam, a great pulpy jam without all the seeds. The rounded bottom pestle, even when you've gone round and round, up and down against the sides, and around some more -- if there is still stuff left in the strainer/chinois, keep moving the pestle up and down to force more pulp and juice out through the bottom third of the strainer. The Winco , 13-7/8'' x 3-1/8'' Wood Chinois Pestle worked great with the New Star Foodservice 537454 Stainless Steel Reinforced Bouillon Strainer, 10-Inch which I bought here (just like my grandmothers): https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0BGT8YYD1?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_titleI purchased this to replace an older version which was cracked. This one is bigger and bulkier which can be a bit tough if your kitchen storage is tight but is effective and seems durable so far.Nice, works great. My husband loves it.Using this with a Chinois in the family since the 1930s to mash annual harvest of choke cherries, goose berries and rose hips for processing and canning into syrup, jellies and jams, this works better than any other method I’ve tried, and requires half the effort to do the work.We bought this to use when straining thick soup. And it works great and is great quality for the price.Looks & feels great to the hand. Mine says made in Vietnam, very good quality. EXCELLENT purchase. I recommended it.If you are going to use a Chinois, this is way more efficient and quick at moving your stock or sauce through the process than using a silicone spatula.Probably the best chinois pestle on the market.Works Great for Stock and also Almond milk.
reviews_1s:
Avoid this and spend the money on a solid wood pestle. This pestle arrived with wood filler in the flaws, biscuit joiners inserted into large voids and a generous helping of wood glue to ensure a solid binding before being sanded down. If your pestle is going to be used to plant plugs in a flower garden, then this will work, however, a broken broom handle will be sufficient for that purpose. Besides you could probably get one for free presuming you didn't purchase the broom. I digress, my apologies. If you are looking to purchase this for food prep, please don't. Come to think of it, the broom handle may be more hygienic.This pestle is made from laminated wood, not from a single, solid piece.
Used it once to strain strawberries through a chinoise.
Carefully cleaned it with warm water and a sponge. Hand dried it with a towel.
When I put it away the next day I noticed that the wood was de-laminating (splitting) along one of the glue joints.
Returned it for refund.
As long as this pestle is made from laminated wood I would not buy it. Period.Attention home canners! This is a well made solid wood product but does not fit the average home canning chinois. Be sure to measure your chinois before ordering. This chinois is very large. Sorry I had to return it.Not very good. The bonding agent for the different pieces that make the object was showing after the first use. Not a solid piece. Feels like it should be sold at ikea. Just buy a steel ladle instead.
